issues.failure_explanation: The proof shows only that each j has some k with a nonzero pairing. It never shows that distinct j use distinct k, so r' >= r does not follow. The claim also fails when singular tubes are supported on different idempotents. If s_{1,1}=e_1 and s_{2,2}=e_2, the single element e_1 U_{:,1}+e_2 U_{:,2} generates both e_1 U_{:,1} and e_2 U_{:,2}, giving a generating set of size 1 < 2. The paper itself later says the image need not be free.

failure_location.quote: The set $\{ \bs{s}_{j,j} \mm \tU_{:,j} \}_{j=1}^r$ is a minimal generating set for $\operatorname{Image}(T_{\tX})$ when considered as $\FFF_n$-module.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the lemma to nonzero singular tubes that are invertible, or to a single idempotent component. Otherwise drop the minimality claim and keep only that the set generates the image.
issues.overall_effect: The stated motivation for the t-rank definition (the number of nonzero singular tubes as a minimal generator count) is unsupported. The later formal results do not use this lemma.
issues.title: Claimed minimality of the generating set is unproved and false in general
issues.why_classification: Repair is a local restriction or weakening of a motivational lemma. It needs a short new argument but leaves the main results intact.

issues.failure_explanation: Length is the largest chain length, so equality needs a chain of exactly ell proper ideals. The proof treats only arbitrary chains and gets lng <= ell. The lower bound is never exhibited, for example via partial sums of the e_j.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the chain 0 ⊂ <e_1> ⊂ <e_1+e_2> ⊂ ... ⊂ R_n of ell proper ideals.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem as stated (equality) is not established by the written proof. The theorem is not used later in the formal chain.
issues.title: Length of tubal ring: proof gives only the upper bound
issues.why_classification: A one-line routine chain construction completes the proof with no change to the statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: establishing Eckart-Young optimality for multi-rank truncation.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof ends after treating multi-rank truncation. For t-rank it never shows that A_r equals a tubal-length truncation, nor that every Y of t-rank <= r has tubal length <= (r,...,r). The multi-rank case also assumes a valid multi-rank r.

failure_location.quote: Then, $\RR_n$ also satisfies Eckart-Young optimality for multi-rank truncations and t-rank truncations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the short argument identifying A_r with tubal-length truncation at (r,...,r) and bounding the tubal length of t-rank-r tensors.
issues.overall_effect: The t-rank half of the claimed implication, and the later statement that the characterization covers t-rank truncation, are not backed by the written proof.
issues.title: t-rank optimality is claimed but only multi-rank optimality is proved
issues.why_classification: The missing step is a routine local reduction to the multi-rank case already proved.

issues.failure_explanation: By Lemma conj.frontal_slices.eq, slices s and s' of a real tensor must be complex conjugates. In the definition of A^(2) the slices are conj(alpha)E_2 and -alpha E_2, which are not conjugate, so A^(2) is not in R_n^{2x2} and is not an admissible competitor. The evaluations also have wrong signs: with alpha=(1-i)/sqrt2, 4 Re(alpha)Im(alpha) = -2, not +2. The two sign errors are not obviously a single typo. The conclusion Im g = 0 is not validly derived as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace A^(2) by a conjugate-symmetric tensor, namely slices conj(alpha)E_2 at s and alpha E_2 at s'. Recompute the two norms and the constant a, then redo the case analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The necessity of Im g_{s',s}=0, hence of orthogonality of the rows of M within one idempotent block, rests on an invalid example. This affects the 'only if' direction of the main characterization.
issues.title: Second counterexample in intra-idempotent orthogonality lemma is not a real tubal tensor and has sign slips
issues.why_classification: The same construction works once the tensor is made conjugate-symmetric and the arithmetic is redone. The method and conclusion survive.

issues.failure_explanation: For M_1=DQ, the quantities beta_r are built from transform-domain energies weighted by mu_k^2, normalized by the weighted ||S-hat||^2. So 1-beta_r is not the original-domain relative error ||X-X_r||^2/||X||^2, which weights slices by mu_k^{-2}. The step is invalid, and so is the conclusion; it also ignores ties in the threshold rule. Counterexample: n=2, m=p=1, M_0-domain singular values (1,1), mu=(10,1), gamma=0.9. Under M_1 the energies are (100,1), so r_gamma(M_1)=1. Under M_0 they are (1,1), so r_gamma(M_0)=2 > 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the statement must be withdrawn or restricted to conditions on mu and the data under which the weighted and unweighted energy orderings are comparable, with a new proof that accounts for the mu-weighting.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed no-go result (normalization always improves compression, scaling is 'necessarily detrimental') is false in general. The related prose in Section 6 and the DMD discussion ('As expected') rests on it.
issues.title: Claim that unit-row normalization never increases r_gamma is false; proof equates transform-domain and original-domain energy
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated, so no comparable unconditional version survives. The practical-implications conclusion must be rewritten with a new argument.
